newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serb leader attacks Moslem president's U.N. speech.
newsitem.headline: Serb leader attacks Moslem president's U.N. speech.

text.p: Bosnia's Serb foreign minister on Thursday condemned a speech to the United Nations by Moslem president Alija Izetbegovic saying it showed he was incapable of leading the country and was against peace.

In a statement faxed to Reuters, Aleksa Buha said Izetbegovic's Wednesday speech "confirms yet again that he is uniquely incapable of leading and representing the three nations living in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina."
He added that it "clearly demonstrates that he is against peace in the Dayton Bosnia (sic)".
"The future... does not seem bright," Buha said.

In his speech to the U.N. General Assembly, his first since he was elected chairman of Bosnia's three-man presidency, Izetbegovic warned of the prospect of renewed conflict if major powers did not do more to enforce the terms of last year's Dayton peace agreement.
All sides -- Serbs, Croats and Moslems -- have accused one another of flouting the agreement.
But international observers have accused the Serbs of clinging to policies that further their dream of a separate state and independent, violating the central pillar of Dayton.
Buha insisted it was the Moslems under Izetbegovic's leadership who are responsible for most of the breaches of the Dayton accord.
